title: Q2 Private Release Waves and Compatibility Gates — Migration Windows & Stakeholder Runbooks
creator: Aisha Thompson
description: Define and sequence Q2 release waves for Private/VPC/on-prem enterprise features with explicit compatibility gates, migration windows, and runbooks for customer success/SE teams. Deliverable includes wave cut definitions (beta, pilot, broad), automated compatibility tests, upgrade rollback criteria, and a stakeholder communications cadence mapped to OKRs. Focus areas: RBAC expansion, KMS/HSM integration paths, private control-plane upgrades, and deterministic schema migrations for persisted KV caches.
acceptance_criteria: Wave definitions documented with scope, eligibility, and success metrics
Compatibility gate checklist implemented and integrated with CI for each wave
Migration windows scheduled with clear rollback criteria and runbook links
Customer communications templates and SE playbooks published
Product and Eng sign-off (Design Review + Security Review) obtained
tasks: Draft wave taxonomy (Beta / Pilot / General Availability) and map to customer segments
Coordinate with Eng to define automated compatibility tests for model runtime and storage schema
Work with Security to complete KMS/HSM threat matrix and gating criteria
Create runbooks for upgrade, rollback, and emergency mitigation for on-prem customers
Schedule migration windows and update Console rollout UI with wave flags
Prepare SE/CS playbook and customer comms templates (email, status page, in-app)
decisions: Adopt wave-based rollout (Beta -> Pilot -> GA) to reduce blast radius
Require passing of automated compatibility suite and manual preflight checklist before Pilot
Use time-boxed migration windows with hard rollback triggers at 2 and 8 hours
Only customers on dedicated capacity may opt out of early waves; on-prem customers need explicit opt-in for Beta
risks: Schema migrations for KV cache could cause tail latency spikes if not coordinated with runtime kernel selection
Customers with strict change freeze windows may miss migration windows and require bespoke support
KMS integrations introduce latency/regional availability dependencies that complicate compatibility gates
Insufficient automated coverage could lead to manual sign-offs slowing rollout cadence
